runs.name: Pentair plc
runs.entry: Price **$52.47** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged; 52-week high $112.13) x **159,637,950 shares** (10-Q cover, 0000077360-26-000045; repurchased shares cancelled, issued equals outstanding) = cap **$8,376M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y par, 2026-10-09). Q1 IN (Pool decides; comparable history from 2018, after the Valves & Controls sale and the nVent spin) · Q2 IN (Pentair a steady 18% to 20% of Pool Corporation's purchases 2014 to 2025; Pool segment margin 27% to 34% 2017 to 2025, above Hayward; the 2026 destock, Pool volume down 46.3% in Q2 while Hayward and POOL rose, written as contrary evidence) · Q3 for (capital-light; growth bought at about 13% after tax) · Q4 weighs against, no STOP (restructuring and transformation costs about $59M every year; the 2025 receivables rise collected) · Q5 integrity IN (the closest call), ability against (the CFO and the Pool CEO left in 2026) · Q6 against (buyback authorizations in dollars with no price; average prices $71 to $100 above every cut range; Taco $1.425B debt-financed, agreed 13 days after the guidance cut; all-stock STOP not met) · **Q7 OUT: owner cash $610.0M a year all-equity (FY2021 to FY2025; $531.1M equity-only; acquisitions $463.7M a year deducted), shown growth 9.08% cut by specific (f) to the 2.62% sales growth; range $36.95 to $49.63 all-equity (net debt $1,514.2M; $37.61 to $48.25 equity-only), width 1.27 to one; the central case returns 4.50% to 5.41% at the price, below the 5.60% Treasury; fair price $13.43 ($17.49 equity-only); Taco beside, added to net debt and credited at nothing, $28.03 to $40.71, fair $4.50.** Run by an interactive batch session, killed after Q5 (f9182279); resumed by the overnight cycle's dispatched analyst, which did not use the first session's uncommitted Q7 draft (written before the 2026-10-10 amendments; committed as a record) and rebuilt Q7 (q7_final.py). The dispatcher re-checked: check_framework PASS; the analyst's check_quotes.py 99 ids, 58 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's own dispatcher_quote_check.py 60 fragments, 0 problems, no E-ids; no tracked research file over 200 KB. Departures owned in the self-audit: Q3 and Q4 in one commit (0dc9b503), Q6 with Q7 (5d69eb1f); the Q4 heading left twice as the first session wrote it; one misquote of [M1994-008] by the first session ('the shareholders' for 'their owners') corrected by the resuming analyst before completion. Framework points for the operator (from the run): amended specific (c) does not say whether the no-growth end charges acquisitions in years one to ten (literal reading taken; the other gives $58.74, above the growth end, the inversion (e) names; the box does not turn on it, the fair price does); specific (f)'s 'highest share of sales in the filings read' when early filings describe a different business; (f) gives no rule for projecting sales; (a)'s growth between successive cycles where only one cycle is comparable; Q6's buyback test against today's range or the range the record supported when the shares were bought; the retention test's market leg ending at the year-end or the price date (opposite answers here). Could not get: Taco's financials (not filed), Fluidra's figures, channel inventory of Pentair stock, a maintenance split of capital spending. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Alert `PNR-v5-fair` at $13.43; the v4.1 bands retired.
runs.narr: A pool-equipment aftermarket sold through one dominant distributor, with margins above Hayward's for a decade, whose 2026 sales fell as the channel worked off Pentair's own 2025 shipments; priced above a narrow range built on growth that was mostly bought. Against: organic growth of about 0.6% a year, buybacks at $71 to $100 just before the price halved, two senior departures, and a $1.425B debt-financed purchase agreed days after the guidance cut.
runs.fair_label: PNR at/below $13.43: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-10 (Test Runs/2026-10-10 Run - PNR Pentair.md; OUT at Q7 at $52.47; $17.49 equity-only; $4.50 with Taco added to net debt). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
